title: RAG with LangChain for Beginners 🚀 | Hugging Face + ChromaDB + Free LLM in Google Colab | Tutorial
author: Cloudsoft Solutions
raw_text: Want to learn **RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) from scratch?** In this beginner-friendly tutorial, we build a **complete ...
summary: this youtube tutorial offers a beginner-friendly, step-by-step guide to building a complete retrieval-augmented generation (rag) system. it walks you through using popular tools like hugging face for models, chromadb for vector storage, and a free llm, all within google colab. rag is a crucial technique that allows llms to access and incorporate external, up-to-date information, making their responses more accurate and specific. learning rag from scratch with practical tools like langchain is fundamental for developing robust llm-powered applications. you could follow along with this tutorial to build your first working rag system, which is a fantastic hands-on project.
why: hands-on rag tutorial with langchain, crucial for building context-aware llm applications.

title: Google doesn't need the LLM crown
author: andsoitis
summary: this title suggests a shift in perspective, indicating that google's strategy with llms might not solely be about having the absolute 'best' or largest model. instead, it could be focusing on integrating llms deeply into its products, services, and ecosystem, or targeting specific applications where a "good enough" model provides immense value. for you, this highlights that the impact of llms isn't just about raw model size or benchmark scores. it's also about how effectively models are applied, integrated, and the overall value they create within a broader system. consider how different companies leverage llms in diverse ways, beyond just competing for the biggest model.
why: shows llm value beyond raw power, focusing on integration and application.
